endorsements.quote: Evaluation should include discrimination, calibration, temporal generalizability, subgroup robustness, interpretability, and decision consequences.

unlisted_practices: Begin AI representation design with a clinical process that existing scores fail to capture rather than with an available sensor stream.
Link digital features to a plausible pathway of functional loss, compensation, adaptation, or recovery.
Test whether a new pathway-based representation adds explanatory or predictive value beyond conventional proxy scores, evaluated against a conventional-proxy baseline.
Perform periodic auditing, recalibration, and explicit versioning of pathway-based representations to keep them provisional and avoid reification.
Use standardized acquisition protocols, feature definitions, metadata, and semantic mappings for cross-site deployment so representations retain comparable clinical meaning.
Keep representational complexity proportional to the clinical question by using the least burdensome set of measurements that preserves the clinically relevant pathway.
Address privacy risk from rich sensor, kinematic, ambient audio, and location data that can reveal information beyond the intended scope of care.
Weigh implementation costs of equipment, personnel training, processing, governance, and maintenance against the incremental clinical value of richer representations.

screen.reason: This is a Perspective paper proposing a conceptual framework (Clinical Reality Translation-Construction) for representational design of AI data in rehabilitation medicine.
